content.title: Jon Jones retires again after Dana White's UFC White House snub: 'No more fighter Jones'
content.text: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC UFC Fri 10 April 2026 15:07 Jon Jones has decided to quit fighting yet again after being unable to land a spot on the White House card this summer.The legendary two-weight world champion is widely considered the greatest fighter of all time, and has held UFC gold at heavyweight and light-heavyweight. He has a loss on his record as a result of a dubious disqualification, but is for all intents and purposes undefeated after facing legends of multiple eras. Tell us what you think about Jon Jones. Is it time for him to retire, or should he fight again in 2026? Jon Jones celebrates winning the heavyweight title at UFC 309. And he has now explained that his gloves are hung up for good after being unable to come to terms.Who is Jon Jones? Inside the life and career of one of the greatest UFC fighters in historyJon Jones retires from fighting again after failing to land UFC White House spotLast summer, Jon Jones made headlines when it was confirmed that he had decided to retire and give up the undisputed heavyweight title to Tom Aspinall without fighting him. His last octagon outing came in November of 2024 at UFC 309 when he knocked out divisional great Stipe Miocic. However, that retirement lasted a matter of weeks before he learned of the UFC White House card for this summer. He instantly returned to training – drafting in Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson and making an active push to land on the historic event.Unfortunately, Dana White seemed adamant from day one that he would not end up on the card, and when it was finally announced last month his name was the most notable absence. Now, he has confirmed to Red Corner MMA that his time in the cage is up and he is moving on to new businesses.“My gloves are hung up, I’m chilling these days,” he explained when asked about potential fights. “You got business, Jon Jones – no more fighter Jon Jones… The businessman, you know what I’m sayin’?”Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Brandon Magnus/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty ImagesUFC Conor McGregor publicly thanks Artem Lobov after settling $6.5 million lawsuit over Proper No. 12 Wed 15 April 2026 17:30 UFC star Conor McGregor can now put his full focus back on a return to the Octagon after the conclusion of Artem Lobov’s lawsuit.The former lightweight and featherweight champion has been inactive since 2021, when McGregor broke his leg against Dustin Poirier at UFC 264.He’s had his eyes on ventures away from the cage but is planning to change that this year, targeting a long-awaited UFC comeback in the summer.And when it comes to dialing in on another fight, the Irishman has eliminated one distraction.LATEST NEWS: Joe Rogan questions one aspect of Nate Diaz vs Mike Perry: ‘Wonder why they agreed on that?’ CHANGE MY MIND: Conor McGregor is the UFC’s greatest legend 'Notorious' took MMA to the next level at the height of his legendary career. Conor McGregor settles with Artem Lobov after being sued over Proper No. 12Former UFC fighter Artem Lobov rose to fame as a teammate of McGregor’s during his journey to multi-weight success in the promotion. Their relationship is far from what it once was, and the pair have even been battling one another on the legal front in recent years.Lobov and McGregor’s feud went public when ‘The Russian Hammer’ sued ‘The Notorious’, claiming a stake in his Proper No. Twelve Irish Whiskey. Lobov took credit for McGregor’s brand, insisting he came up with the idea and provided key ideas and research on the matter. The Russian admitted he had turned down McGregor’s $1 million offer after the company’s success, alleging that he’d been promised five percent “no matter what” by his ex-teammate.Lobov sued for that share, which would have amounted to $6.5 million of the $130 million reportedly taken home by the UFC star when McGregor sold Proper No. Twelve for $600 million.The case was due to commence on Wednesday in the High Court and was scheduled to last eight days. However, Lobov’s attorney Andrew Walker told the judge that a settlement had been reached and a trial was no longer required.“I want to thank him for his hard work for my whiskey business,” McGregor said in a statement after the settlement (h/t Irish Independent).The Russian opted not to issue a statement after the settlement, details of which were not disclosed.LATEST NEWS: Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39Photo by Brandon Magnus/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty ImagesMcGregor’s attorney Mark Lyman read his statement to the court, which included a comment about how the ex-UFC champ is now looking forward to focusing on his training for “this summer’s fight.”His UFC return is not yet confirmed but is reportedly slated to headline International Fight Week in July, with Max Holloway the frontrunner to welcome him back to action.Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty ImagesUFC Mike Perry reveals ‘incredible’ UFC fighter he’s training with to prepare for Nate Diaz on Netflix Wed 15 April 2026 17:00 Mike Perry is getting work in with an electrifying UFC lightweight ahead of his return to mixed martial arts.Perry will be among the top names competing on the card for Netflix’s very first MMA event on May 16.Before Ronda Rousey headlines against Gina Carano, Perry will face Nate Diaz as both men make their MMA comebacks after a number of years away.Many who predict a victory for Diaz envision ‘Platinum’ being submitted, and Perry has revealed who he’s training with to hopefully stop that from happening.LATEST NEWS: Joe Rogan questions one aspect of Nate Diaz vs Mike Perry: ‘Wonder why they agreed on that?’ Nate Diaz or Mike Perry? Mike Perry is training with UFC fighter Terrance McKinney ahead of his MMA return against Nate DiazFor Perry, the five-round welterweight clash at Inglewood’s Intuit Dome will mark his first time competing in MMA since a loss to Daniel Rodriguez spelled the end of his UFC tenure in 2021.Since then, the 34-year-old has fought exclusively in striking-only realms, becoming a star in the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship and also sharing the ring with Jake Paul in boxing.With that in mind, Perry admitted that getting back into MMA training has been somewhat of a shell shock during a recent appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show.Fortunately, ‘Platinum’ has a prominent UFC star helping him gear up for the Diaz showdown.“It’s been tough,” Perry said.“I’ve been doing really good on diet and taking care of my body, stretching, ice tubs, getting chiropractic work.“The grappling aspect, I get to work with really great fighters at Fusion X-Cel in Ocoee, Florida,” he continued. “I’ve been working a lot with Terrance McKinney. He’s an incredible athlete, an incredible fighter.“He goes for broke, but then in the gym, he’s so calculated, and he’s such a good wrestler and grappler. It’s been great working with Terrance. His MMA skills are fantastic.”LATEST NEWS: Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39Copyright 2021 Getty ImagesMcKinney knocked out Kyle Nelson in just 24 seconds at UFC Seattle last month.The lightweight fighter now has 17 first-round finishes in 18 professional wins in mixed martial arts, with eight coming in the UFC Octagon.Fans will see if his habit of fast starts has rubbed off on Perry in training when he shares the cage with Diaz on May 16.Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC/Zuffa LLC via Getty ImagesMMA Ronda Rousey uses Jon Jones double standard to reject concern over her making MMA comeback aged 39 Wed 15 April 2026 16:00 Ronda Rousey will end her long mixed martial arts layoff nine months before she turns 40.Netflix will look to make an immediate splash in MMA on May 16, when the streaming giant stages a stacked card promoted by Jake Paul’s Most Valuable Promotions at Inglewood’s Intuit Dome.The main event will see Rousey return against fellow pioneer Gina Carano, with those two headlining following comebacks for a few other MMA stars like Nate Diaz and Francis Ngannou.Many have focused on the age of the card’s top names, particularly in the case of Rousey vs Carano.LATEST NEWS: Joe Rogan questions one aspect of Nate Diaz vs Mike Perry: ‘Wonder why they agreed on that?’ Who wins when Ronda Rousey and Gina Carano return to face each other? They both are old.pvadodariaFeatured commentI am more interested in the Ngannou fight, personally.1 Ronda Rousey shuts down age discussion for her MMA return against Gina CaranoRousey’s knockout loss to Amanda Nunes in December 2016 was her last fight in the cage. After over nine years away, ‘Rowdy’ turned 39 in February.Carano, meanwhile, is coming off an even longer layoff. The ex-Disney star has not fought since 2009, when she was knocked out by the legendary Cris Cyborg in Strikeforce.Despite their veteran status, Rousey thinks it is unfair for critical fans to be focusing on their ages, especially when the same scrutiny is not given when it comes to the likes of Jon Jones.“I never hear Jon Jones’ age being brought up as a disqualifying factor,” Rousey said during an appearance on CBS Mornings.“It’s not like my ovaries are fighting, you know what I mean?“Why are we even talking about this?”LATEST NEWS: Alexander Volkanovski is certain he knows what Carlos Ulberg’s injury is and when he’ll be backPhoto by Hans Gutknecht/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty ImagesRonda Rousey was warned about fighting at her age by CM PunkWith those remarks in mind, the former UFC women’s bantamweight champion likely wasn’t pleased to see a prominent name recently bringing up her age.During an interview with talkSPORT in February, CM Punk reacted to Rousey’s MMA return, having attempted to find success in the sport himself at a similar point.“I think it’s great. We’re going to find out if she’s still got it,” CM Punk said.“I think fighting at an older age — trust me, I am an expert on this — it’s not the easiest thing to do.“But she’s fighting somebody who is age comparable, who also has had a long layoff,” he added.“They’re both big names, both big superstars. I think people are going to tune in to watch this — and I know I will.”Join Our NewsletterReceive a digest of our best Bloody Elbow content each week direct to your mailbox
